DES CAS availability-selected pilot — 2026-10-20

Run 20261020T173805630133Z_b5f7d0d3, method cas_discrete_v2; both original S profile names retained. Table SHA-256: 11e4eeb76b92a11447281dad217098d0280d98c27db60c1d99b1471cc1e6fbc9.

The sample is the union of 75 candidate IDs with precomputed products in the local nucleated_lsbg legacy-fliplr object-centered 1024-pixel output tree. It is an availability sample from the 84,200-row candidate catalog, not a representative LSBG population or a confirmed-galaxy sample. No CAS-based selection was made. All 225 requested object-band rows are retained, including 63 absent images. Source files were read without modification or an additional image flip.

The HTML report includes all variants, finite-only sample quantiles, missing counts and flag frequencies. statistics.csv gives p16, median and p84; these describe this selected sample, not measurement errors.

Measured behavior

Median C is 2.538 (g), 2.588 (r) and 2.645 (i); median raw A is 0.775, 0.728 and 0.787 respectively. These large raw asymmetries cannot be interpreted as intrinsic disturbance without noise calibration. Only 2/66 g, 2/66 r and 29/30 i images have valid sky corrections. In i, 17/29 corrected A values are negative; the median is −0.044. The g/r corrected samples are too small for distribution or correlation conclusions. Corrected subsets are not representative of the available sample.

In the symmetric synthetic scene with zero PSF smoothing, median raw A rises from 0 to 0.073, 0.243 and 0.482 as noise sigma rises from 0 to 0.5, 2 and 5. The corresponding corrected medians are approximately 0, −0.007, −0.053 and −0.121. This exposes negative bias under these controlled settings; sky subtraction alone does not recover zero asymmetry at high noise. No DES error bar or noise calibration is inferred from these three-seed experiments.

The division by ten above removes only the Conselice normalization. Remaining differences also reflect the kernel size and excluded central radius; they do not establish which profile is better. Correlations use paired finite rows. band_comparisons.csv likewise uses only common object IDs in each band pair; independent g/r/i distributions have different sample membership.

Raw S rank correlations between profiles are 0.994 (g), 0.988 (r) and 0.968 (i). After dividing Conselice S by ten, median paired differences remain −0.080, −0.071 and −0.086 respectively, consistent with the profiles measuring different residuals and regions. Rank agreement does not validate either definition.

Input and quality checks

The sheet selects g-band objects at the minimum, median and maximum full-image mask fractions. Cyan marks the catalog WCS center; orange marks the measured CAS aperture. It is an illustrative visual inspection, not an exhaustive target segmentation validation.

All 162 existing image-mask pairs have identical target WCS positions, target positions within 0.5 pixel of the stamp geometric center, and an unmasked target pixel. The runner also checks WCS agreement on a 3×3 grid across each stamp. The masks contain 0/1/2 values in g/r (overlapping upstream mask contributions) and 0/1 in i; all nonzero values are contaminants. WCS agreement establishes alignment between stored arrays, not an independent astrometric calibration. mask_diagnostics.csv records the mask fraction inside each measured aperture and the most valid of the four corner tiles. Median aperture mask fractions are 2.6% (g), 7.2% (r) and 8.2% (i), with maxima 27.7%, 36.7% and 49.9%. The median best-corner valid fraction is 93.85% in g/r, below the 95% criterion, and 100% in i. This explains the band dependence in missing corrections without requiring a claim about the galaxies' intrinsic structure. Better blank-region selection should be evaluated as a separately versioned sky method.

The upstream legacy horizontal flip has not been reinterpreted or reapplied. FITS DATE-OBS normalization warnings occurred; no data arrays were altered.

Flags: {"no_clean_sky_tile": 129}. Errors: {"missing_cutout": 63}.

Controlled sensitivity experiment

sensitivity.csv contains 144 deterministic synthetic measurements: symmetric Gaussian and offset-clump scenes, PSF sigma 0/1/2 pixels, noise sigma 0/0.5/2/5, three random seeds and an injected masked contaminant variant. The target Gaussian has peak 40 and sigma 12 pixels; the offset clump has peak 12, sigma 2. All metrics, including Petrosian radius and center, are remeasured in every case. sensitivity_summary.csv gives medians across the three seeds. These are stress experiments with known scenes, not a DES noise or PSF calibration. Three seeds are insufficient for quantitative uncertainty estimates. A masked scene also removes some genuine galaxy light under the contaminant footprint.

Continuing the analysis

There is no execution or data-access blocker for the next methodological stage. The existing 162 images support testing a sky-region search throughout the stamp, while retaining the corner-only v2 results as a baseline. A new version should compare sky coverage and correction stability on the same objects, exclude the target aperture and contaminants, and use matching rotation/interpolation in sky and galaxy measurements. More synthetic noise realizations and DES-specific injection experiments can then quantify bias and PSF sensitivity.

The 63 missing image-band combinations limit coverage of this availability sample; they do not prevent work on the existing images. Representative population claims require a broader sample. Reference-code matching and uncertainty calibration constrain interpretation, rather than preventing exploratory analysis. No external permission or additional input is needed to start these checks on the available data.

Interpretation limits and next validation

The corner-only sky estimator often cannot find a ≥95% valid 32-pixel tile in these masked fields. Missing corrections remain null. The corrected subset therefore has additional selection bias. Negative corrected values are retained. The cleanest-corner choice, integer-aligned sky rotation versus subpixel galaxy rotation, noise, PSF, target-mask extent and discrete apertures may bias values. No morphology classes or published CAS thresholds are assigned. Both A outputs and both S profiles remain necessary for subsequent calibration.

Matched statmorph/historical implementation agreement and DES-specific injection recovery, PSF matching and uncertainty calibration remain unperformed. These are required before physical classification or population conclusions. The present report establishes end-to-end execution and exposes limitations of this pilot.

Reproduction

Install this repository and its declared test dependencies, then run:

python scripts/prepare_des_pilot.py --output .outputs/des_inputs_new
python -m algorithmic_morphology run --config-file-name .outputs/des_inputs_new/config.py --chunk-size 15
python scripts/validate_sensitivity.py --output .outputs/sensitivity_new
python scripts/analyze_pilot.py --run-dir <completed-run-directory> --inputs .outputs/des_inputs_new --sensitivity .outputs/sensitivity_new --output <new-report-directory>

The preparation script accepts --source-project and --catalog for other local locations. The exported config records the actual local paths. Run manifests record package versions, code hashes, catalog/config fingerprints and numerical settings; table rows contain image/mask SHA-256. The run began with uncommitted fixes, so code hashes, rather than its base git commit alone, identify the code.

The run_source/ directory preserves all five package source files exactly as used in the real run, verified against the manifest hashes. Subsequent runner hardening makes git metadata optional and fsyncs the latest-symlink directory; neither changes numerical measurements. manifest.json references checkpoint parts in the original local run directory; the portable export contains the canonical table rather than duplicating those partitions. Plot regeneration:

python scripts/plot_pilot.py --report-dir reports/des_pilot_20261020
